name: Status badges
summary: How to show the state of a domain object with <aha-status-badge>: one box, four looks, a dot, an icon or no marker, one marker family per dimension, the default badge for information that is not a status, and when a badge is the wrong element.
highlights: One box, four looks, three markers
Never mix dot badges with icon or no-marker badges in one dimension
Default badge for counters and types; due dates are plain text
lead: A status badge tells the state of a domain object (a survey, a presentation, a course, a learner) in one glanceable, screen-reader-announced token. Every badge is the DS element <aha-status-badge>, so the box, the four looks and the markers stay the same in every app. This guideline says which look and marker a state takes, what must never be mixed, and what is not a badge at all.

skillRef.note: The DS owns this ruleset. The component contract (contracts/status-badge.json) carries the element API; this guideline carries the composition rules; the judge criteria and evals live in anti-slop/.

surfaceChoice.useFor: the lifecycle state of a survey, presentation or collector
surfaceChoice.example: Published, Draft, Closed, Archived with a dot

surfaceChoice.useFor: how far a learner or a course has got
surfaceChoice.example: Completed (check), In progress (hourglass), Not started (no marker)

surfaceChoice.useFor: a state with no built-in status, dressed in one of the four looks
surfaceChoice.example: Invited (draft look), Joined (closed look), Removed (archived look)

surfaceChoice.useFor: information that is not a status, in the default look
surfaceChoice.example: 4/6, a slide type with its icon, Unanswered or Time out with an icon

composedOf.use: the badge itself: <aha-status-badge> with status, look, marker and icon
the 12px icon marker, called by name from the registry through the badge's icon attribute
the published look background, with --aha-text-link for the label and --aha-vivid-pink-100 for the dot
the draft, closed and default look background (--aha-gray-25 for archived)
the contrast target: a free-form label the user adds, removes or filters by is a Tag, not a status badge
the contrast target: a count bubble or notification dot on another element is a Badge, not a status badge

rules.rule: Render a status badge only for a value from a known status enum (lifecycle, progress, membership). A free-form label is a Tag; a count bubble or notification dot is a Badge.

Every badge is <aha-status-badge>. Set status for a built-in state, or look (published, draft, closed, archived) for a state the element does not know. Never hand-build the pill, restyle a Tag, or override the box (22px tall, 8px side padding, 6px radius, 12px semibold label, 6px gap).

A state takes one of four looks: published (pale pink, pink label) for the live or successful end state; closed (grey, default ink) for an ongoing or ended-normally state; draft (grey, muted label) for not begun or not yet live; archived (lighter grey, disabled label) for retired or removed. No status gets a hue of its own: no green, red, amber or blue.

A badge has one marker before the label or none: a 6px dot for lifecycle states; a 12px icon from the DS icon registry in place of the dot; or no marker. Progress uses the built-in set: Completed is the published look with system-check, In progress the closed look with system-hourglass-high, Not started the draft look with no marker. Never a dot and an icon together.

Never mix the dot variant with the icon or no-marker variants inside one status dimension (one column, one list, one card slot, one legend). A dimension shows dots only, or icons and no-marker badges only. A state added to an icon dimension takes an icon or marker="none".

Information that is not a status but sits where badges sit (a counter such as 4/6, a slide or question type with its icon, Unanswered, Time out) uses look="default": the same box, Gray 35 background, default ink, with or without an icon, never a dot.
A due date or deadline is not a badge. Write it as plain text; use the primary colour only when it needs attention (due soon, due today, overdue) and do not highlight on-time states.

An app that already owns an approved colour set for a result (Report: Correct, Partially correct, Incorrect) keeps those colours and takes only the box, through --aha-status-badge-bg and --aha-status-badge-fg set once in its stylesheet. Never use the two properties to tint a lifecycle or progress status, and never inline a hex on a badge.
The visible label is always sourced from i18n (t(`survey_status.${status}`) or the object's own namespace), in sentence case. Never hardcode the visible string.
Adding a state means adding a translation key AND choosing its look and marker in one mapping (one place per enum), so the same state never appears in two looks.
The element carries role="status" and an aria-label equal to the visible label (the DS element sets both). The text label is always present; a dot or an icon is decorative and never the only signal.
Existing screens on the aha-status-pill class convention keep working and are migrated to the element when they are next touched; new work never adds that markup.

reuseNote: Doc-only guideline. The component it describes ships as <aha-status-badge> (contracts/status-badge.json, lib/aha-status-badge.js) and is gated there.

selfCheck.label: every badge is <aha-status-badge> with a status or a look; the box is not overridden
each status dimension uses one marker family: dots only, or icons and no-marker only
counters, types, Unanswered and Time out use the default look, never a dot
no due date or deadline is drawn as a badge
no status has its own hue; colour comes from status or look, no inline hex
label from i18n; role=status + aria-label match the visible text
